newsitem.title: USA: Media General seeks regional leadership.
newsitem.headline: Media General seeks regional leadership.

text.p: Media General Inc Chairman , President and Chief Executive Stewart Bryan on Tuesday said he saw himself as the Rupert Murdoch of the Southeast.

With considerably fewer financial resources than the Australian media magnate, Bryan said he hoped to steer Media General on a path of providing news and information in a single region of the United States through a variety of formats, including television, newspapers and online services.
"We're the poor man's Rupert Murdoch," Bryan said during a conference call with reporters in which he discussed Media General's purchase of Park Acquisitions Inc for $710 million.

Ultimately, Bryan said he envisioned creating newsrooms that would be shared by journalists working in more than one medium. The first spot may be in Tampa, Florida, where the company owns a television station and a newspaper, he said.
"We are looking forward to that," he said.

As part of the Park deal, the company added 10 network-affiliated television stations, 28 daily community newspapers and 82 weekly newspapers. At the same time, it shed a number of media properties from outside the Southeast.
That left the company with only one media outlet outside the region -- WUTR, an ABC-affiliated television station in Utica, N.Y. Bryan said the company planned to sell that station, too.
"We have some negotiations going on at the moment," he said.
Except for the Utica station, the company's only stake outside the Southeast is a 40 percent interest in the Denver Post newspaper.
Bryan said the company embarked on its strategy about 18 months ago, when it decided to become the "leading provider of information ... in the southeastern United States."
Its mission was influenced in part by what Bryan described as a general uncertainty surrounding the media industry.

"We are uncertain as to what the viewer, the reader, the consumer of news and information, what he or she will want in the future," Bryan said. "and we think by concentrating our resources in one geographic area ... that we will be able to provide this news and information in whatever form the consumer wants it."
Through its acquisition of Park, Media General has increased its television saturation of households by 145 percent, it said, reaching one out of every four viewing households in the region.
The chairman portrayed the transaction as the culmination of a nine-year restructuring of the company -- "a return to the basics, if you will," Bryan said.
He also believes that by strengthening the company's regional presence, Media General would position itself well to pursue electronic publishing possibilities.
The company already has an online newspaper in Tampa, called Tampa Bay Online, and one in Richmond, called Gateway Virginia.

"We hope to be able to provide all of the news and information that can be provided locally by these news-gathering outfits and also be the catalyst for bringing together other kinds of information for people who want it online," he said.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1709))
